title: Feature-selection protocol, binary target, amendment 1 (development data only)
supersedes: FS-1 (identical procedure, three researcher-defined trust levels). FS-2 changes only the target: the datasets' own binary label 'malicious' (0 = benign, 1 = malicious), because trust levels are now derived from the model's risk score in the decision layer.

iot23.selection_rows_meaning: validation rows from scenarios wholly unseen in that fold's training data (scenario_group == 'whole_scenario')

rt_iot2022.selection_rows_meaning: all validation rows (no scenario/session/device identifier exists)

selection_criterion.metric: macro_F1 over the two dataset classes benign/malicious (labels 0,1; zero_division=0)
selection_criterion.model_combination: per-fold mean of the Random Forest and XGBoost measuring instruments
reported_but_never_used_for_decisions: per-class F1 (benign, malicious) on selection rows

unit_of_selection: original variable (a categorical variable's one-hot columns are kept or removed together)

filters_unsupervised_fit_on_all_developm.constant_numeric: drop numeric variables with min == max
filters_unsupervised_fit_on_all_developm.rare_level_rule: a categorical level becomes a dummy column if p(1-p) > 0.01 in ANY listed rarity population; levels failing all populations are dropped (rows with them get all-zero dummies); a categorical variable with no surviving level is removed

correlation.tie_break: of the most correlated pair, drop the variable with the larger mean absolute correlation with all remaining variables (findCorrelation logic, Kuhn & Johnson); repeat until no pair exceeds the threshold
correlation.exclude_reason: destination port is a nominal identifier coded as an integer; rank correlation with it is not meaningful

ranking.method: grouped permutation importance (Gregorutti et al., 2015): all columns of a variable are permuted together with one shared row permutation
ranking.score: macro_F1 on selection rows of the held-out fold
ranking.importance: baseline score minus mean permuted score (unclipped)
ranking.combination: mean importance across folds per instrument, then mean of the two instruments
ranking.nesting: for each outer fold f, a ranking R_f is computed using ONLY folds other than f (train on folds not in {f, g}, measure importance on fold g, for every g != f). The feature-count curve for fold f uses R_f, so no fold's own labels influence the ranking it is evaluated with. The final ranking R uses all folds (train on folds != g, measure on g, for every g).

count_selection.candidate_counts: every count if <= 10 variables survive the filters, otherwise about 10 evenly spaced counts always including the full set
count_selection.curve: for each count n and outer fold f: train both instruments on folds != f using the top-n variables of R_f; score on the selection rows of fold f
count_selection.rule: one-standard-error rule: SE = sample SD (ddof=1) of the best count's per-fold scores / sqrt(K); select the SMALLEST count whose mean is >= best mean - SE
count_selection.final_variables: top-n of the final ranking R

diagnostics_not_used_for_decisions: Nogueira et al. (2018) stability of the top-n sets across the K nested rankings
pairwise Kendall tau between nested rankings
mutual-information ranking of the filtered variables (stratified sample of at most 200000 development rows) and its Spearman correlation with the permutation ranking
rank and per-fold importance of id_resp_p (destination-port ablation is a later, separate predeclared step)
amendment: FS-2 applied as frozen selected ONE IoT-23 variable (proto, two 0/1 columns): the one-standard-error rule was uninformative because the between-fold standard error of the best count (0.176) was about half its mean (0.376) and the nested rankings disagreed (Nogueira stability -0.10; Kendall tau 0.02-0.13). A model on a single two-level variable can output at most three distinct risk scores, so it cannot provide the graded risk score the decision layer needs to form a Suspicious band. FS-2.1 therefore keeps ALL variables that survive the unsupervised filters for IoT-23 (no performance-based count selection); the count curve is still computed and reported. RT-IoT2022 is unchanged (one-standard-error rule; stability 0.86). Decided on development results only; no test data used.
